title: Data sovereignty sync topology and TTL controls for analytics events
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Implement a region-aware replication topology and tenant-level data residency controls for Console usage analytics. The goal is to ensure analytics events belonging to tenants that require regional residency are either stored and processed only in their allowed regions or are reduced to metadata-only replication when cross-region storage is restricted. This ticket covers schema changes, replication topology, TTL controls for transient artifacts, encryption/KMS mapping, routing logic, and a staged rollout plan with backfill and monitoring.
background: Current analytics pipeline aggregates Console events (route usage, latency spans, feature flags usage) into a centralized US-primary Kafka cluster and then runs batch jobs and real-time consumers from that cluster. Customers with data residency requirements (EU, UK, APAC regulated tenants) have asked that tenant data remain within a designated region. Past tickets implemented tenant tagging at ingest, but we lack a robust, testable replication topology and enforcement controls (TTL, metadata-only flows) that satisfy legal/regulatory constraints and operational SLOs.
technical_design: Overview: introduce a region-aware replication graph and per-tenant residency policy enforcement in the analytics ingestion and streaming layers. Key components: 1) Ingest layer: augment event envelopes with 'tenant_region_policy' and 'tenant_allowed_regions' fields and persist to a write-ahead topic in the local region. 2) CDC/Replicator: use Kafka Connect based replicator with filtering plugins to either: a) replicate full event payloads to allowed regions, b) replicate only metadata (non-PII payload removed) to regions where full storage is disallowed, or c) suppress replication entirely for strictly local-only tenants. 3) Topic topology: create per-region topics with explicit naming convention analytics.<region>.<logical_stream>. Partitions are keyed by tenant_id for affinity. 4) Routing: Console backend's analytics router service will consult Residency Service cache (tenant->policy) to decide ingest target region and whether to remove payload before writing to the global bus. 5) Schema and metadata: introduce v2 envelope schema with residency flags and schema registry compatibility policy. 6) TTL controls: consumers and downstream sinks must honor per-tenant TTLs; implement server-side retention override via topic configs + sink-side enforcement (S3 lifecycle + hotstore compactor). 7) KMS/encryption: map tenant->region->KMS-key. Replicator ensures payloads encrypted with the destination-region KMS key upon write. 8) Observability: new metrics: replication_lag_{tenant,region}, cross_region_egress_bytes, residency_violation_count, replicator_filter_drop_count. Dashboards and alerting rules defined in console-analytics-monitoring doc. 9) Backfill: backfill job will selectively rehydrate regional topics for opted-in tenants using watermarking and idempotent writers. 10) Failover: in case of regional outage, fallback policy controlled per-tenant: deny, replicate to fallback-region (with masking), or queue for later backfill. Trade-offs: maintaining per-tenant partition affinity increases topic count and operational overhead but simplifies compliance checks and per-tenant enforcement. Filtering at replicator reduces risk of accidental cross-region copies but adds processing latency.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Residency Service exposes tenant policy and Console router consults it for every analytics write (unit/integration tests). 2) A test tenant marked EU-only results in payloads only landing in eu-* topics or metadata-only copies to other regions (end-to-end test). 3) Replicator plugin correctly strips payload fields listed as PII and logs stripping events (test harness verifies payload absent). 4) New schema v2 registered and backward-compatible for consumers; no consumer failures in staging. 5) Backfill job can rehydrate 100k events/hr per worker with idempotency guarantees and watermarking. 6) Monitoring: replication_lag and residency_violation_count dashboards populated and alerting at set thresholds. 7) Security review completed with KMS mapping and threat model signed off.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag and schema registration in staging. Phase 1: Deploy ingest envelope v2 in staging with Residency Service cache seeded. Phase 2: Deploy replicator filtering plugin in staging and run dark-traffic replicates for 2 weeks; validate metrics. Phase 3: Enable for opt-in internal tenants and one low-traffic EU customer in a controlled window; monitor for 72 hours. Phase 4: Gradually enable for more tenants, run backfill for historical windows with throttling. Phase 5: GA: turn feature flag on for all tenants requiring residency. Phase 6: Post-GA, run a final cleanup to retire central-only topics and update runbooks. Each phase gated by automated checks: no residency violations in last 24h, replication_lag < 5s for real-time streams, and cross_region_egress within budgeted limits.
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema handling, replicator filter logic, and CLI backfill dry-run. Integration tests: end-to-end staging pipeline with synthetic tenants for EU/US/APAC, asserting correct topic placement and KMS encryption. Chaos tests: simulated regional broker outage to validate failover policy and backlog behavior. Load test: verify per-partition throughput with tenant-keyed partitions and measure latency regression (<10% on P95). Security tests: verify that PII fields are never present in disallowed regions via automated scanning of replicated topics.
migration_steps: 1) Register v2 envelope schema; consumers opt-in to handle v2. 2) Deploy Residency Service cache and seed from tenant metadata export. 3) Deploy ingest library that writes v2 envelopes behind feature flag. 4) Enable replicator in metadata-only mode for target regions to validate filter correctness. 5) Run backfill on small tenant segments and validate. 6) Flip feature flag for full replication for compliant tenants. 7) Gradually scale backfill. 8) Deprecate v1 after a monitoring window and consumer sign-off.
observability_and_sla: SLO targets: replication_lag P99 < 2s for real-time streams in normal conditions; replication_lag P99 < 30s for nearline/backfill scenarios. Alerts: residency_violation_count > 0 triggers pager immediately for workspace-security on-call. Dashboards: per-tenant replication map, cross-region egress, replication filter action logs. Runbook: step-by-step to investigate and remediate a residency violation (immediate quiesce, revoke downstream retention, start blind backfill).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidentally replicating PII to an unauthorized region. Mitigation: multi-layer enforcement: ingest-side masking, replicator filtering, and destination KMS enforcement plus automated scans. Risk: increased operational complexity (topics and config sprawl). Mitigation: templated infra-as-code for topic creation and per-tenant policy UI in Console for visibility. Risk: replication lag under heavy load. Mitigation: dynamic throttling, autoscaling replicator workers, and per-tenant rate limits. Risk: KMS key availability cross-region. Mitigation: pre-provision keys and a documented emergency fallback key with strict audit and manual gating.
next_steps: 1) Approve security review ticket and KMS mapping doc. 2) Spike: implement a minimal replicator filter that strips three PII fields and run dark traffic in staging (owner: Sanjay). 3) Create IaC templates for per-region topics and retention override (owner: Ingrid Ma). 4) Prep canary tenant cohort and coordinate with Solutions Eng for customer opt-in windows.
